topic: The Rhythm of Mathematics: Understanding Music and Measure Theory
target_audience: High school students interested in music theory and STEM

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time
lecture_lines: Music relies on a steady pulse called the beat.
Fractions represent how long each note lasts.
A whole note lasts the full beat.
animations: Create a glowing pulse line representing the constant beat (#FFD700).
Display a 'Whole Note' circle and divide it into halves (#00CED1).
Further divide the halves into quarter notes (#FF6347).

sections.title: Defining the Measure (The Container)
lecture_lines: Measures organize beats into defined containers.
Time signatures define the capacity of each measure.
Think of it as a musical basket.
animations: Draw an empty rectangular 'Measure Basket' frame (#FFFFFF).
Animate numbers '4' and '4' appearing as a fraction (#00FF00).
Animate a 'Full' indicator appearing when notes fill the frame (#FF4500).

sections.title: Visualizing Measure Theory
lecture_lines: Notes fill measures like water in a vessel.
Each note occupies specific rhythmic space.
They must sum to the measure's total capacity.
animations: Display a robot arm placing blocks of varying lengths (#1E90FF).
Visualize the total width equaling '4' units perfectly (#ADFF2F).
Final frame shows a completed, locked '4/4' measure box (#FFD700).

sections.title: Dynamic Application: Changing Meters
lecture_lines: Different time signatures change the musical feel.
A 4/4 march feels structured and heavy.
A 3/4 waltz spins in a circle.
animations: Show a character jumping on a 4-beat march track (#FF6347).
Show a character jumping on a 3-beat waltz track (#9370DB).
Morph the track shapes between square (4/4) and triangle (3/4) (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Beat is the unit of time.
Measure is the container for notes.
Time signature sets the rhythmic rule.
animations: Draw a sine wave moving across the screen (#00CED1).
Align peaks of the sine wave with measure start lines (#FFD700).
